title.en: No Men Are Foreign (James Falconer Kirkup)

text.en: Beneath every uniform, a single body breathes like ours.

The poet reminds us that no men are strange and no countries foreign. Beneath all uniforms a single body breathes like ours, the land others walk on is earth like ours, and they too are aware of sun, air and water.
The poem says we must not hate people because they belong to another country or speak another language. All people are part of the brotherhood of men, and to fight against others is unnatural, a fight against ourselves.
Notice the repeated idea of sameness and the use of we and our. Learn the words brethren, harvest and foreign.
